title: Prescription Insurance on File Patient Pay on a Re-Billed Cash Fill
content:
## Definition

Under **Prescription Insurance on File**:

1. **The re-billed cash fill** is the patient's most recent fill paid in cash.
2. **The re-bill rate** is the patient pay per day of the most recent claim re-billed on the coverage, that is, its patient pay divided by its days supply. When no claim has been re-billed on the coverage, the re-bill rate is 0. The rate itself is not rounded.
3. **The patient pay** of a re-billed cash fill is the re-bill rate multiplied by the days the cash fill supplied, rounded to the cent, and never more than the cash the patient paid for the fill. The rounded amount is compared with the cash paid, and the lower of the two is the patient pay.

"Re-billed on the coverage" means a claim on the coverage's claim ledger paid on the retroactive re-bill basis; the most recent is the latest such claim.

## Worked figures (hypothetical records)

The most recent re-billed claim on the coverage shows a patient pay of 18.75 for 30 days: the re-bill rate is 18.75 divided by 30, which is 0.625 per day.

| Cash fill's days supply | Cash paid | Rate multiplied by days | Rounded | Patient pay |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 30 | 40.00 | 18.75 | 18.75 | 18.75 |
| 20 | 40.00 | 12.50 | 12.50 | 12.50 |
| 12 | 40.00 | 7.50 | 7.50 | 7.50 |
| 30 | 10.00 | 18.75 | 18.75 | 10.00 — held to the cash paid |

With no re-billed claim on the coverage, the rate is 0 and the patient pay is 0.00.
